question: The Kudremukh mines of Karnataka are primarily associated with extraction of which mineral?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Iron ore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kudremukh mines** in Karnataka are primarily associated with the extraction of **iron ore**.
 
• Kudremukh is located in the **Chikkamagaluru district** of Karnataka and is known for its rich deposits of **magnetite iron ore**, one of the best quality ores found in India.
 
• The **Kudremukh Iron Ore Company Limited (KIOCL)**, a government undertaking, was established to exploit the iron ore deposits in this region.
 
• Iron ore from Kudremukh was mainly exported to countries like **China** and **Japan**, contributing significantly to India's export revenue.
 
• The mining operations in Kudremukh were stopped in **2005** due to environmental concerns, as the area falls within the **Kudremukh National Park**, a biodiversity hotspot.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Iron Ore in India:**

 
 
• India is one of the world's leading producers of iron ore, with deposits found in states like **Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Karnataka, and Goa**.
 
• India's iron ore is primarily used for steel production, which is vital for infrastructure development and industrial growth.
 
• Key types of iron ore found in India include **hematite** and **magnetite**, with hematite being the most abundant and widely used.
 
 
 
• **Kudremukh National Park:**
 
 
• The Kudremukh National Park is part of the **Western Ghats**, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• It is known for its unique biodiversity and serves as a habitat for various endangered species like the **Malabar civet** and the **Indian leopard**.
 
• Due to ecological concerns, the Supreme Court of India ordered the cessation of mining activities in this region in **2005**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact of Mining:**
 
 
• Mining activities often lead to deforestation, soil erosion, and loss of biodiversity, especially in ecologically sensitive zones like the Western Ghats.
 
• Efforts are being made to promote sustainable mining practices and restore degraded ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Iron Ore Exports:**
 
 
• India exports iron ore mainly to **China**, which is the largest consumer of iron ore globally, followed by countries like **Japan** and **South Korea**.
 
• Iron ore exports contribute significantly to India's foreign exchange earnings but are subject to fluctuations in global demand and prices.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Magnetite vs Hematite:**

 
 
• **Magnetite** contains higher iron content (up to 72%) compared to **hematite**, which contains around 50-60% iron.
 
• Magnetite is preferred for steelmaking due to its high iron content and lower impurities.
 
 
 
• **Western Ghats Ecology:**
 
 
• The Western Ghats are among the eight "hottest hotspots" of biological diversity in the world.
 
• They play a crucial role in regulating the monsoon and are a source of numerous rivers in southern India.
